targets.body_markdown: **Experimenter-confirmed mapping correction.** The construct labels below supersede the earlier Test 2 labels. The source wells, RFU readings and endpoint calculations are unchanged; column 12 is Blank, whose composition is not documented. This is a relabelling of the same acquisition, not an independent experiment. ### What was measured Test 2 contains **72 observed wells**: six stimulus rows × twelve construct positions. Its archive key is `odor-2026-10-21`; the source exports record 21 October 2026 with no timezone. It is distinct from Test 1, the four-acquisition assay, and its column order must not be transferred from that assay. Rows B/C were not supplied here; they are not gain-based exclusions from this dataset. | Row | Addition | Supplied preparation | |---|---|---| | A | VUAA1 | 1:100 dilution | | D | Isopentyl acetate | 1:1,000 dilution | | E | 2-Heptanone | 1:1,000 dilution | | F | Valeric acid | 1:1,000 dilution | | G | Pentyl acetate | 1:1,000 dilution | | H | DMSO vehicle | 0.1% DMSO | The user reports 0.1% DMSO for the solutions. These preparation facts are retained as supplied; absolute molar concentrations cannot be inferred from dilution factors alone. The older assay's nominal VUAA1 concentration is not reused here. | Column | Condition | Corresponding composite | |---|---|---| | 1 | Or7a + ORCO | [BBa_26ZAGFK0](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26zagfk0#odor-2026-10-21) | | 2 | Or19a + ORCO | [BBa_2629NIWH](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-2629niwh#odor-2026-10-21) | | 3 | Or42a + ORCO | [BBa_26Q1Q094](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26q1q094#odor-2026-10-21) | | 4 | Or98a + ORCO | [BBa_26TZLBMJ](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26tzlbmj#odor-2026-10-21) | | 5 | Or22a + ORCO | [BBa_26WOX4B1](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26wox4b1#odor-2026-10-21) | | 6 | Or67a + ORCO | [BBa_265G8CE1](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-265g8ce1#odor-2026-10-21) | | 7 | Or67b + ORCO | [BBa_269VSDDR](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-269vsddr#odor-2026-10-21) | | 8 | Or59b + ORCO | [BBa_26Y7CI2H](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26y7ci2h#odor-2026-10-21) | | 9 | Or85b + ORCO | [BBa_26K1TU11](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26k1tu11#odor-2026-10-21) | | 10 | Or35a + ORCO | [BBa_26LLF3LM](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26llf3lm#odor-2026-10-21) | | 11 | ORCO only | [BBa_26E11Z80](https://registry.igem.org/parts/bba-26e11z80#odor-2026-10-21) | | 12 | Blank | Composition not documented; no part assigned | ### Primary calculation: change within post-addition fluorescence minus change within pre-addition fluorescence For each well, use the first and last actual reading in each acquisition: - **ΔF_pre = 100 × [F_pre(48 s) / F_pre(0 s) − 1]**, in percent. - **ΔF_post = 100 × [F_post(168 s) / F_post(0 s) − 1]**, in percent. - **S = ΔF_post − ΔF_pre**, in percentage points (pp). pre-addition fluorescence has five readings at 12 s intervals and post-addition fluorescence has fifteen. This subtracts the observed baseline-stage disturbance from the observed within the post-addition acquisition fluorescence change. It uses separate denominators for the two stages. No baseline line is extrapolated to 168 s, and no rate, peak value or mean post-addition fluorescence/pre-addition fluorescence ratio is substituted for these endpoints. The primary S windows are unequal: **48 s of pre-addition fluorescence versus 168 s of post-addition fluorescence**. Therefore the data also include **S48 = 100 × [F_post(48 s)/F_post(0 s) − 1] − ΔF_pre**, using equal 48 s windows. S48 is a sensitivity view of the recorded data, not an independent replicate or evidence that the longer-duration result is incorrect. The separate vehicle contrast is **S(stimulus,c) − S(H,c)**. A further blank-control contrast subtracts the corresponding vehicle contrast in column 12. These are differences between individual wells, with shared references; they remain dependent descriptive comparisons. Vehicle subtraction is additional to the primary within-well drift subtraction. ### Relation to Test 1 Test 1 had four acquisitions: a baseline before the blank addition, the blank round, a baseline before the test addition and the test round. Its retained calculation uses peak-three fluorescence changes and subtracts the blank-round excursion. Test 2 has only pre-addition fluorescence and post-addition fluorescence. **S is not the Test 1 R metric**, and these results are not pooled as replicated measurements of a single statistic. The Test 1 values remain unchanged and separately defined in their original tables. The mean-ratio metric **100 × (mean post-addition fluorescence / mean pre-addition fluorescence − 1)** remains in the historical mean-ratio audit. It describes a different question and no longer supplies the main response conclusion. An post-addition fluorescence trajectory can rise even if its entire acquisition lies below the earlier pre-addition fluorescence acquisition. Source timestamps do not identify the injection time, so no continuous injection-aligned trace is inferred. ### Reproducible inputs and limits There is one observed well per condition–addition pair. Five baseline readings and fifteen subsequent readings are within-well sampling, not twenty biological replicates. Numeric acquisition settings, stock molarities, addition-to-read delay and clone/culture lineage are not independently established from these exports. Within-stage normalization avoids making the between-acquisition level offset the response metric; it does not establish the biological cause of the trajectory. ### Post-addition dynamics compared with DoOR The retained Test 2 post-addition fluorescence records were reanalysed using each well’s first-three and last-three mean (0/12/24 s and 144/156/168 s). D = L/E − 1 and C = D_odor − D_DMSO for the same supplied channel; 100C is reported in percentage points. This post-addition dynamic metric is distinct from baseline-subtracted S and VUAA1-referenced N, and is a reanalysis rather than an independent experiment. The supplied post-addition fluorescence workbook channel mapping and source-cell provenance are retained. DoOR consensus minus receptor-specific spontaneous firing rate was compared with C separately for each odorant. Pearson r / Spearman rho: 2-heptanone +0.317/+0.406; isopentyl acetate +0.325/+0.442; valeric acid +0.211/+0.283; pentyl acetate −0.002/+0.006. n=10 receptors except valeric acid (n=9; missing Or42a reference). ORCO-only and blank controls are not included in tuning-OR correlations. Thus three odorants show weak positive correspondence and pentyl acetate is near zero. One well per condition and a shared vehicle reference constrain interpretation; positive C can mean less decline than DMSO. No independent replicate, significance claim, receptor-specific activation, or trained odor-classifier validation is inferred. [Two comparison figures and full discussion](https://2026.igem.wiki/nthu/results#f1-dynamic-door). Test 2 measures **the Or19a+ORCO co-expression condition associated with this receptor module** across six additions, mapped to **column 2**. The condition label links the measurements to the team's expression system; it does not independently confirm the clone sequence or membrane localization. This is a system-level observation, not an independent assay of a bare CDS or isolated reporter domain. The supplied preparation is 1:1,000 odorant dilution, 1:100 VUAA1 dilution and 0.1% DMSO. Stock molarities and the underlying formulation are not independently recoverable from the exports. The [shared methods](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-methods) give the full construct/stimulus mapping, calculation and provenance. ### Test 2: corrected changes and VUAA1-referenced responses ![Or19a: Test 2 corrected changes S and construct-matched VUAA1 reference ratios N](https://registry.igem.wiki/documentation/0be83e89-d65a-4d12-8d16-ed29c4a90798/3c206318c2433be06063af6cad8af1c1b4f65b7d45367958a1a8b56b9cbf580e.avif) *Upper panel: S = ΔF_post − ΔF_pre, in percentage points (pp), using the observed post-addition fluorescence change over 168 s and pre-addition fluorescence change over 48 s. Lower panel: N = (S − DMSO S) / (VUAA1 S − DMSO S), the same dimensionless normalization used in the Results heatmap. DMSO is 0 and VUAA1 is 1 by definition; these anchors do not bound other responses. Negative values remain visible. Each condition–addition pair is one separate well.* ΔF_pre = 100 × (last pre-addition fluorescence / first pre-addition fluorescence − 1); ΔF_post = 100 × (last post-addition fluorescence / first post-addition fluorescence − 1). **S = ΔF_post − ΔF_pre**, in percentage points (pp). S48 repeats the calculation using only the first 48 s of post-addition fluorescence and the full 48 s of pre-addition fluorescence; it is a window sensitivity check, not an extra replicate. The separate DMSO-well contrast is shown alongside S rather than replacing it. | Well | Addition | ΔF_pre (%) · 48 s | ΔF_post (%) · 168 s | S (pp) | S − vehicle S (pp) | S48 (pp) | |---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | A02 | VUAA1 | -2.27 | +6.67 | +8.94 | +9.43 | +6.13 | | D02 | Isopentyl acetate | -2.52 | -2.54 | -0.01 | +0.48 | +1.26 | | E02 | 2-Heptanone | -2.41 | -2.27 | +0.14 | +0.63 | +0.95 | | F02 | Valeric acid | -2.80 | -1.81 | +0.99 | +1.48 | +1.64 | | G02 | Pentyl acetate | -2.04 | -2.27 | -0.23 | +0.26 | +0.90 | | H02 | DMSO vehicle | -2.66 | -3.15 | -0.49 | +0.00 | +1.39 | ### Interpretation **Reading S and N together.** For this construct, VUAA1 has **S = +8.94 pp** and the separate DMSO well has **S = -0.49 pp**. Their difference is **+9.43 pp**, so the VUAA1 ratio is **N = 1.000**. The value 1 in the Results heatmap is this reference ratio, not a corrected change of 1 pp. The bars, the accompanying table and the heatmap use the same Test 2 endpoints; no response values were changed to produce this display. For VUAA1, the within the post-addition acquisition change is **+6.67%**, while pre-addition fluorescence changes **-2.27%**. Their disturbance-corrected contrast is **S = +8.94 pp**. The DMSO well has **S = -0.49 pp**, giving a separate vehicle difference of **+9.43 pp**. The matched-duration sensitivity value for VUAA1 is **S48 = +6.13 pp**. S answers whether the recorded post-addition fluorescence trajectory changes more than the recorded pre-addition fluorescence trajectory. It does not compare the absolute mean post-addition fluorescence level with the preceding mean pre-addition fluorescence level. Those acquisitions can begin at different fluorescence levels, so a rising post-addition fluorescence trace and a lower post-addition fluorescence mean are compatible. The earlier mean-ratio calculation remains in the historical audit summary (retained in the source archive with its superseded labels) and is not the primary response measure here. The two windows differ in duration (168 s versus 48 s), so S is not a matched-duration rate correction. This screen contains one observed well per condition–addition pair; repeated readings do not supply independent cultures. Positive S means post-addition fluorescence changes more, or decreases less, than pre-addition fluorescence; it need not imply a raw post-addition fluorescence increase. It is not proof of receptor-specific activation, calcium influx, selectivity or a detection limit. Negative values are not classified as inhibition. The [exploratory VUAA1-referenced supplement](https://registry.igem.org/collections/40067138-a3dd-4e5b-b8a4-50b097ee0156#odor-2026-10-21-vuaa1-reference) rescales the separate odorant-minus-DMSO contrasts by this condition's VUAA1-minus-DMSO contrast, **+9.43 pp**. It retains the S values above and does not measure or correct per-well transfection efficiency. ### Post-addition dynamic response A separate reanalysis of the retained post-addition fluorescence readings uses the supplied post-addition fluorescence workbook channel labels and source-cell map. For **Or19a**, the odorant-minus-DMSO contrasts are **2-heptanone: +1.16 pp; isopentyl acetate: +0.62 pp; valeric acid: +1.30 pp; pentyl acetate: +0.90 pp**. Each well is normalized to its first-three-reading mean; the contrast subtracts the matched channel’s DMSO late-to-early change from the odorant change (last-three mean / first-three mean − 1). This metric uses post-addition fluorescence only and is distinct from S and VUAA1-referenced N above; it does not replace those calculations or supply an independent biological replicate. VUAA1 is retained as reference data without division or threshold selection. One well represents each condition. A positive contrast can reflect less decline than DMSO; it does not establish receptor-specific activation. The experimenter confirmed this post-addition fluorescence channel mapping; it supersedes the earlier Test 2 receptor labels, without changing the raw measurements. [Full dynamic-response/DoOR comparison and interpretation](https://2026.igem.wiki/nthu/results#f1-dynamic-door) · [Analysis and validation source](https://gitlab.igem.org/2026/software/nthu/aerosense/-/tree/main/code/aerosense/wetlab/odor-f1-dynamic).
